reasons: Numeric warning signals (aggregate of R01-R19): all 4 of 4 computable models fire (Beneish M-score, Dechow F-score, accruals, cash flow vs income). Every quantitative earnings-manipulation screen agreeing is a strong signal: high accruals and weak cash conversion relative to reported income are among the most predictive markers of misstatement.
Disclosure red flags (aggregate of F01-F28): 7 of 24 possible flags present, roughly 29%. That is elevated rather than extreme, and it supports the numeric signals without being decisive alone.

Limitations: the card gives only aggregate counts, with no individual F or R values, so I cannot tell which flags fired (e.g. auditor change, restatement, material weakness) or how large the ratio deviations are. The score is therefore moderated from the very high range a full 4/4 numeric sweep would otherwise suggest.
